title: Mangwobe, Sachem of Rockaway
summary: Mangwobe was a mid-seventeenth-century Rockaway sachem named in the July 4, 1657 Hempstead boundary conference.
content:
Mangwobe was a mid-seventeenth-century Rockaway sachem named in the July 4, 1657 Hempstead boundary conference. That record places him in diplomacy with leaders from Massapequa, Montaukett, Merrick, and neighboring communities, but the cited sources do not establish his birth or death dates.

His appearance connects Rockaway leadership with Tackapousha of Massapequa, Wyandanch of Montaukett, Merrick village representatives, and English officials at Hempstead.12

Historical Context

The 1657 meeting revisited ancestral land boundaries and claims tied to earlier transactions, showing that western Long Island land questions involved several Native communities and not only one town or deed.1

The record for Mangwobe is brief. A later 1682 Rockaway petition uses the spelling Mongowack, but the available evidence is not strong enough to treat that as the same person here.1

References

  1. John A. Strong, The Algonquian Peoples of Long Island from Earliest Times to 1700, p. 222.
  2. Sandi Brewster-Walker research document dated April 19, 2017.
why_this_matters: Mangwobe keeps Rockaway leadership visible in western Long Island land history. His brief but important record shows that Merrick, Massapequa, Rockaway, Montaukett, and Hempstead boundary questions were connected through Native diplomacy.
